tier_reason: First-party Boost docs relative-time tables (GNU C++ 10.3.0, GMP 6.2.0, Boost 1.78, run 2021-09-30) vs gmp_int; no flags, no CPU model and no benchmark source linked from the page, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 128-bit: cpp_int(fixed) beats gmp_int on operator* (1 vs 4.80 relative time), operator+(int) (1 vs 4.98), operator+ (1 vs 5.87), operator- (1 vs 3.44), operator^ (1 vs 1.35), construct (1 vs 5.62). 256-bit: cpp_int(fixed) wins +, -, ^, construct (gmp_int 1.45, 1.25, 1.01, 1.53) but loses operator* (1.77 vs gmp 1) and operator+(int) (1.73 vs gmp 1).
corrections.caveats: Docs from 2021-09-30 (GCC 10.3.0, GMP 6.2.0, Boost 1.78); CPU and flags not stated; 500,000 ops per test excluding allocation/copy. Win limited to small fixed widths: GMP wins 256-bit * and +(int), larger sizes, and Miller-Rabin on 128-bit numbers by ~11x (mpz_int 0.00443s vs cpp_int 0.0497s on the int_real_world page).

notes: Record overstated the 256-bit result: gmp_int wins 256-bit operator* and operator+(int). Metadata verified (BSL-1.0, 263 stars, last commit 2026-09-24). Miller-Rabin numbers are on perf/int_real_world.html, not the benchmark_url page.
